newsitem.title: CHINA: China's communists invoke Deng Xiaoping.
newsitem.headline: China's communists invoke Deng Xiaoping.

text.p: Deng Xiaoping's personality cult is stronger than ever just days before Beijing resumes sovereignty over Hong Kong.
China's propaganda machine is eulogising the late paramount leader, whose 1984 deal with Britain ensured the handover of Hong Kong at midnight next Monday.
Diplomats say the Hong Kong handover offers President and Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin an opportunity to roll out his most powerful ideological weapon.

The official People's Daily on Friday splashed on its front page a photograph of Deng with Jiang, his anointed successor, by his side during a meeting in Beijing in 1990 with a group empowered to draft Hong Kong's post-colonial constitution.

The newspaper, mouthpiece of the Communist Party, this week took off its hat to Deng with a front-page headline screaming: "The Revered Mr Deng is Great!" under a photograph of a huge portrait of Deng erected in Shanghai.
"For (the Communist) Party, Deng remains the most valuable ideological asset," a Western diplomat said.
"They have decided to play him up," said the diplomat.

Deng who died last February aged 92 concocted the "one country, two systems" formula by which Britain agreed to hand Hong Kong back to China and Beijing promised the enclave would keep its capitalist lifestyle for 50 years.
Britain took Hong Kong after defeating imperial China in the 19th-century "opium wars".

"The (Chinese) leadership came to the conclusion some time ago that it really is not feasible to try to play down Deng's contributions to economic development or... the reform process," the diplomat said.

Deng led China out of an age stunted by Maoist ideology and Stalinist central planning, pulling tens of millions of Chinese out of absolute poverty and opening up opportunities to make or lose fortunes in a market economy.
"Deng Xiaoping has become an ideological pillar on which the legitimacy of the party rests," an Asian diplomat said.
The Communist Party, in power since 1949 and plagued by a string of corruption scandals, has seen its popularity dive in recent years.

One Chinese analyst said the party was bolstering Deng to shore up President Jiang's position before a crucial party congress in the second half of this year when the new post-Deng leadership line-up will be decided.

The People's Daily said officials across China were deepening their study of Jiang's speech last month in which he urged cadres to hold high Deng's great banner of building "socialism with Chinese characteristics".
"Socialism with Chinese characteristics" is the fig-leaf phrase Deng coined to justify such un-Marxist concepts as free markets, private enterprise and stock exchanges.

"To hold high the banner of Deng Xiaoping's theory to build socialism with Chinese characteristics... we must resolutely safeguard the authority of the collective leadership with comrade Jiang Zemin as core," the People's Daily said.

Jiang, the Chinese leader who will formally take back Hong Kong at midnight next Monday, is using Deng as a charm to ward off attack from power-hungry party elders and political rivals, diplomats said.
